# Gap fill: juice, shake, hit-stop, satisfaction, feedback latency studies (2020+)

Scope: gaps (a) to (e) from `p5-p6-p7-juice-repeat-sound.md` and `p1-composition-camera-attention.md`. Kao CHI 2024 and Kao 2020 were not re-done (assigned elsewhere). Field framework terms used as in the first run: gameplay, shape, value, colour, timing, composition; windup, punch, crescendo, follow-through, dissipation.

## 1. Search count used

WebSearch: 13 of 15 used. WebFetch: about 45 calls, many of them OpenAlex or arXiv API queries (metadata and abstracts only). Several full texts were fetched as PDF binaries and converted with pdftotext. Semantic Scholar returned 429. Publisher pages for Royal Society, SSRN, ACM and HAL returned 403 or an Anubis block.

## 3. Gap-by-gap results

### GAP: (a) 2021-2026 peer-reviewed or preprint juice / visual feedback studies (n, design, effect sizes)

Status: PARTLY FILLED [V: confirmed]. Several new controlled studies found, but all except G3 and G4 only at abstract level. No second CHI/FDG-scale (n>1000) study found besides Kao 2024. No 2021-2023 juice experiment in IEEE CoG or Entertainment Computing surfaced in the indexes I could query (OpenAlex title search for "juic" 2021+ gave no further games papers beyond the ones listed).

| finding | numbers | evidence level | source ids |
|---|---|---|---|
| Vibrotactile juice improved player experience; low and high juicy haptics each beat none; low vs high not different (except HX expressivity) | n=38; within-subjects; 6 versions (haptics none/low/high x visual low/high) of Breakout; PXI, HX, enjoyment. No stats on page | study | G2 | [V: confirmed - low and high each beat none; low vs high not different except HX expressivity; no stats on page]
| Particle effects and text effects both raised PXI Appeal over no-effect; combined text+particles scored highest (not above Juicy Particles) | n=45 within-subjects. | Juice did not change click performance (time to click, accuracy) in the observation and performance stages | no significant differences. Read as a mostly-null result with two small material-stage exceptions, not proof of no effect]
| Preference after the study | 44.4% Particle, 40% Text+Particle, 11.1% Text, 4.4% No Effect (n=45) | study | G3 | [V: confirmed]

Takeaway for the agent (inference): the one fresh dose-response test (G4 study 3) found no gain from none to high, while Kao 2024 (first run) found amplification reduced effectance and competence. Add what G4 shows on timing: put the reward beat after the action. This matches "punch then follow-through" and does not support "more is better".

### GAP: (c) Hit-stop perception

Status: PARTLY FILLED [V: confirmed]. One peer-reviewed duration study read in full (n about 16, one game). A second study (IEICE 2023, 0.1-0.2 s) is a search-snippet only and is NOT counted.

| finding | numbers | evidence level | source ids |
|---|---|---|---|
| Sword/bow action game, 8 hit-stop levels from 0.0 to 0.7 s (playback speed during hit-stop 0.01x): longer hit-stop was more uncomfortable overall. Votes for the most enjoyable level averaged 0.37 s (Scene 1, sword) and 0.39 s (Scene 3, sword+bow); votes for the most stressful averaged 0.56 and 0.57 s. Pleasant/unpleasant boundary 0.537 s (Scene 1) and 0.55 s (Scene 3) | n=16 (Scenes 1, 2) and 15 (Scene 3); one-vote-per-participant histogram, Mahalanobis boundary. Scene 2 (bow) was non-normal and got no boundary | study (small n, one custom game) | G10 | [V: confirmed - 0.37/0.39 s and 0.56/0.57 s are means of per-participant top-vote histograms, boundaries 0.537 and 0.55 s, n 16/16/15, s=0.01 playback, Scene 2 non-normal. Wording: "enjoyable average" is the mean of most-enjoyable-level votes, not a measured optimum]
| The unpleasant duration depended on weapon context (bow vs sword) | exact bow numbers not given in the text read | study | G10 | [V: corrected - no bow boundary exists since Scene 2 was non-normal; treat "depended on weapon context" as weak, unverified]
| Hit-stop length that varied with gaze duration (within the comfortable range) raised sense of impact vs a constant 0.39 s; enjoyment also higher for most dynamic functions | Phase 2 n not stated in the pages read; 4 functions plus constant reference; no statistics read | study (weak reporting) | G10 | [V: unverified - not re-checked]
| Games with no hit-stop sit at the bottom of the impact-feel ranking; those that have it vary length by attack strength. Sound delay between visual and audio feedback is named as ruining immersion (a player-comment finding, not measured in ms) | 2 of 16 games lacked hit-stop (rank 39th and 40th), under 70% positive impact comments; GG Xrd 7 frames light, 10 heavy | preprint (observational) | G9 | [V: unverified - G9 and GG Xrd talk not re-opened here]
| Hit-stop for others: observers of a VR player's hit-stop felt uncomfortable at the unpredictable movement | only named in a search answer, not opened | not counted | (snippet) |

Takeaway (inference): the 0.37-0.39 s "enjoyable" averages in G10 are much longer than the 7 to 10 frame (about 117 to 167 ms at 60 fps, computed in the first run) fighting-game practice. Both can be true because G10 measured "which of 8 levels feels best" in a sword action game with near-frozen playback, not matched to attack strength. Treat 0.54 s as an upper bound for discomfort in that game, not a target.

### GAP: (d) "Satisfying" perception studies (completion, closure, predictability), peer-reviewed

Status: STILL OPEN for closure and completion. PARTLY FILLED only indirectly: three peer-reviewed results touch predictability, expectation, and timing alignment as sources of pleasure. No empirical peer-reviewed study of "oddly satisfying" stimuli found (OpenAlex 2019+ "oddly satisfying" returned media-studies, culture and ethnography papers only).

No source found that measures "closure" or "completion satisfaction" of a physical or visual event (for example a stack finishing its collapse). Not found: any ms or size parameter.

Status: PARTLY FILLED [V: confirmed]. Strong game-specific effect data for 25 to 120 ms delays; perceptual threshold numbers are mostly second-hand and pre-2020; only audio latency has a 2024 JND study (abstract level).

|---|---|---|---|

| Audio delay in an FPS: tension and negative affect rise with delay; 40 ms had no effect, 270 ms raised tension | n=24; 0, 40, 270, 500 ms. (This is first-run S9; the first run's corrected statistics stand) | study | G13 | [V: unverified - abstract not opened here]
| Expectation alone changes felt latency: with true latency fixed at 75 ms, telling players it was 120 ms (vs 30 ms) lowered competence, raised tension and cut performance | n=24 experienced CS:GO players (>=100 h); displayed 30/60/90/120 ms. | Out-of-sync sound after a visible hit is a named cause of low impact-feel rank, not measured in ms | One Punch Man: A Hero Nobody Knows low rank | preprint (observational) | G9 | [V: unverified]
| Roblox-specific input-to-feedback latency | no number found | none | n/a |

Takeaway (inference): for a mobile Roblox game, the first visible/audible response to a tap should be in the same frame as the input where possible; different, varying delays (jitter between weapons or devices) hurt more than a steady small one (G11). Delay perceived as a function of expectation (G12) means loading the player with "laggy" cues can itself feel slow.

Do not average these; they test different things. |

| `p5` S9 row (first-run) | Confirmed: G13 abstract matches (n=24; 0, 40, 270, 500 ms). The first-run correction on "270 ms lowered positive affect" was not re-checked here. |

## 6. Still open and how to test it ourselves

| gap | status | self-test in Studio |
|---|---|---|
| n, intensity values and effect sizes of Lin and Tanaka 2026 (screen shake and agency) | open | Ask owner for the PDF via a university or open-access route (RSOS says CC-BY; our fetch was blocked). Until then use only the direction. |
| Upper limit of shake before it hurts comfort (flat screen, mobile) | open | One blast at 3 shake strengths and 2 durations; owner rates comfort after 10 blasts; use Epic/Sleitnick presets from the first run as anchors. |
| Hit-stop length per attack strength for brick destruction | open | Test 0, 50, 100, 150, 250 ms freezes on a weapon hit; owner picks per weapon tier; Roblox can freeze only the weapon animation and particles, not physics (first-run inference). |
| Feedback position in time (before, during, after the action) | partly | Hold the effect set fixed and shift the big sprite burst: on contact vs 100 ms later; owner A/B. G4 predicts post-action works better, but that was a dashboard UI. |
| Closure / completion satisfaction (for example a tower finishing its fall) | open | Log a short "tail" of settle and dust after the last brick lands vs cutting at the last hit; ask owner which feels finished. |
| Roblox audio-visual and input latency | open | Frame-count a screen recording of a touch to the first sprite frame on a mid phone; compare 1 frame vs 3 frame start. Test constant vs jittered weapon delay (G11 predicts jitter is worse). |
| Hit-stop with a second 2023 source (IEICE 0.1-0.2 s for knock-back attacks, 0.2-0.4 s for slow motion) | snippet only | Fetch the IEICE PDF from a Japanese network or ask owner; do not use the number until opened. |
